subject: Re: Comparative sizing analysis — isolated GPU footprint for St. Mercy Health
messages:
From: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@stmercy.org>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stmercy.org, Rajat Verma <rajat@cloudops.consulting>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated vs Private: request for footprint and cost guidance

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this call last week. Procurement and our cloud team need a concise comparison between Redwood Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in Redwood-hosted infra) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem private deployment) specifically for our PHI workloads. We are targeting a first-phase deployment supporting clinical note summarization and secure search, with peak concurrent users estimated at 120 active sessions during business hours (~8am-6pm).

Key asks:
- Rough GPU count for each model tier (open LLM base + 7B and 70B variants) for both Dedicated and Private options.
- Differences in operational overhead and lead times (e.g., dedicated capacity provisioning vs private VPC/on-prem installs).
- A conservative cost delta and any requirements for isolation (network, SOC2 evidence, HSM/KMS).

Can you provide a short memo and a spreadsheet we can share with finance by EOD Monday?

Best,
Michael
Procurement | St. Mercy Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@stmercy.org>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private: request for footprint and cost guidance

Michael —

Thanks, this is exactly the kind of framing that helps. I can get you a concise comparison and an initial sizing workbook. Quick clarifying Qs to make the estimate useful:

1) Latency SLOs: are you targeting 99th percentile <300ms for single-turn generation, or is slightly higher (500–700ms) acceptable for the clinical NLP pipeline?
2) Model preference: do you plan to run a single larger model (70B) or have a split strategy (7B for classification/embeddings, 70B for generation)?
3) Data residency: will all inference traffic be routed through their VPC / on-prem network (i.e., no egress of PHI outside St. Mercy)?

Prelim notes:
- Dedicated: good fit if you want Redwood-managed infra with reserved throughput and quicker time-to-serve. We can reserve predictable GPU pools (A100/H100s), enable an isolated tenant, and apply strict network peering + KMS. Typical lead time for reservation is 2–4 weeks depending on region and inventory.
- Private: required if your policy forbids PHI leaving customer-controlled network or you need fully air-gapped on-prem. Private has longer lead times (3–8 weeks for VPC setup; on-prem longer depending on hardware procurement) and higher operational lift for updates and model rollouts.

I’m looping Marcus for a sizing pass and an initial spreadsheet. If procurement needs it, we can include SOC2 artifact pointers and a minimal MRA.

I’ll send a draft workbook in the morning.

——
Grace O'Connor

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@stmercy.org>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private: request for footprint and cost guidance

Michael / Grace —

Attaching an initial sizing workbook (st-mercy_sizing_spreadsheet.xlsx) and a brief runbook. High-level summary below; numbers assume 120 concurrent active sessions, average request length ~800 tokens, and a mix of short-generation (summaries) and embeddings for search.

Model profiles and conservative GPU counts (provisioning + buffer):
- 7B models (FP16 / int8 friendly) — target for embeddings and classification:
  * Dedicated: 2 x A10 / L4-class nodes (or 1 A100 40GB with partitioning) to handle 120 concurrent lightweight requests with batching; supports autoscaling burst to 3 nodes.
  * Private: 2 x L4 equivalent or a single smaller rack of L4s; operationally similar but customer-managed.
- 70B dense model (generation) — higher memory and latency sensitivity:
  * Dedicated: 4 x A100 80GB (or 2 x H100 80GB if using sharded launch) for steady-state with conservative KV-cache for session pinning. This gives room for 40–60 concurrent heavy generation sessions with batching tuned to SLOs.
  * Private: 3–5 x H100/A100 depending on on-prem networking and whether you accept slightly higher batching latency. Private deployments require attention to NUMA, RoCE settings, and rack-level networking for sharded models.

Operational overhead / differences:
- Dedicated: Redwood handles kernel optimizations, runtime updates, and automatic prefix caching. We recommend a dedicated isolated pool for St. Mercy with committed capacity and a smaller burst pool as fallback.
- Private: Customer (or partner) needs to run the control plane connectivity and schedule OS/kernel updates; Redwood offers an install package and optional managed support. Patch windows and change approvals add friction to model rollouts.

Cost delta (order-of-magnitude guidance, monthly):
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $XXk–$YYYk/month (depends on GPU type and region). Assumes committed monthly capacity and includes managed runtime.
- Private (VPC-managed with customer-owned hardware): higher upfront capital for hardware + ongoing ops; monthly OPEX depends on whether Redwood manages the control plane. If St. Mercy purchases GPUs, we’d provide a support contract (typically $Zk/month plus per-token usage).

Security & compliance items to include in your procurement packet:
- SOC2 attestation summary and evidence pointer (soc2-evidence.pdf)
- Dataflow diagram showing PHI isolation and minimal egress (can embed in the workbook)
- KMS/HSM integration notes and key custody model

Attachments referenced: st-mercy_sizing_spreadsheet.xlsx (workbook with per-model rows), soc2-evidence.pdf, mra_template.docx

Next steps / recommended ask for procurement:
1) Confirm latency SLO (99p target) and preferred model split (7B/70B mix).
2) Approve a two-month committed dedicated pool (recommended) to shorten lead time; hold private engagement in parallel if final policy requires on-prem.
3) Schedule an architecture readout next Wed with Redwood infra and St. Mercy network/security teams.

Happy to refine the workbook after getting the SLOs.

— Marcus
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Michael Thompson <michael.thompson@stmercy.org>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stmercy.org, Rajat Verma <rajat@cloudops.consulting>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private: request for footprint and cost guidance

Grace / Marcus —

This is great, thank you. A few clarifications from our side after an internal review:

- Latency: 99p <500ms is acceptable for now, but for some clinician-facing flows we want to eventually tune toward <300ms.
- Model split: start with the mixed approach you suggested (7B for embeddings/classification, 70B for generation).
- Residency: must remain in our VPC for PHI; egress of raw PHI to Redwood-hosted public infra is a non-starter.

Procurement is comfortable starting with a 60-day committed Dedicated pool if Redwood can demonstrate clear network isolation and KMS integration. We will run legal/infosec sign-offs in parallel on Private deployment options.

One ask from security: can Redwood provide a short checklist of what we must supply for a private VPC install (VLANs, jumpboxes, hardware firewall IPs, HSM connectivity)? That will speed approvals.

I’ll expect the spreadsheet shortly and will circulate it to finance.

Michael

Michael / team —

Thanks — wrapping up the workbook and a one-page memo for finance (attached). Quick summary and ask so procurement can proceed:

Summary:
- Recommended near-term path: 60-day committed Dedicated pool sized as follows: 2 L4-class nodes for 7B workloads + 4 A100 80GB equivalent for 70B generation. This keeps dataflow inside St. Mercy VPC via private peering and uses customer KMS (no raw PHI egress).
- Why Dedicated first: fastest path to production, predictable latency, and Redwood-managed runtime reduces ops burden.
- Private path: proceed in parallel for long-term on-prem or air-gapped requirements; expect longer lead time and higher upfront cost.

Action items for procurement:
- Approve 60-day committed Dedicated pool estimate (I’ll attach the cost worksheet).
- Provide a named contact from networking/security to receive the Private install checklist (we’ll send a 1-pager: VLAN, port, jumpbox, HSM endpoint, NTP, certs).
- Confirm HubSpot/PO reference number so Stephanie can generate a draft order and include SOC2 artifacts.

I’ll attach: st-mercy_sizing_spreadsheet.xlsx and a 1-page memo for procurement. Stephanie, can you prepare a draft order and price sheet for the 60-day commit?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Grace
